paper_title: Adapting General-Purpose Embedding Models to Private Datasets Using   Keyword-based Retrieval
caption: Retrieval performance of MAP@10 for different m and sampling strategies.

model_annotations.Bulgarian: The provided bar chart illustrates the retrieval performance measured by MAP@10 for two distinct sampling strategies—Fine-to-Coarse Sampling Strategy and Uniform Sampling Strategy—across five different values of m, specifically m=6, 7, 8, 9, and 10. The horizontal axis, labeled “m”, represents the discrete categories being compared and is arranged in ascending numerical order from left to right. The vertical axis, labeled “MAP@10”, quantifies the performance metric and is scaled linearly from 23.0 to 27.0, with tick marks and grid lines spaced at intervals of 0.5. The chart employs a grouped bar layout, with each value of m having two adjacent bars: a purple bar representing the Fine-to-Coarse Sampling Strategy and a yellow bar representing the Uniform Sampling Strategy. For each m value, the purple bar is consistently taller than the corresponding yellow bar, indicating higher MAP@10 scores for the Fine-to-Coarse strategy. The purple bars for m=6, 7, 8, 9, and 10 have approximate heights of 26.0, 26.7, 26.3, 26.6, and 26.5 respectively, while the yellow bars for the same m values have approximate heights of 24.4, 24.8, 25.6, 25.3, and 24.4 respectively. The bars are not visually emphasized through special formatting such as shading or bolding, and the legend in the top right corner clearly distinguishes the two sampling strategies by color.
model_annotations.English: This bar chart illustrates the retrieval performance measured by MAP@10 for two distinct sampling strategies—“Fine-to-Coarse Sampling Strategy” (purple bars) and “Uniform Sampling Strategy” (yellow bars)—across five different values of the parameter m, which are labeled 6, 7, 8, 9, and 10 along the horizontal axis. The vertical axis, labeled “MAP@10”, is scaled linearly from 23.0 to 27.0, with tick marks at regular intervals of 0.5. For each value of m, there are two adjacent bars representing the respective sampling strategies. The purple bars, corresponding to the Fine-to-Coarse strategy, are consistently taller than the yellow bars for the Uniform strategy across all m values. Specifically, for m=6, the purple bar reaches approximately 25.9 and the yellow bar reaches approximately 24.4; for m=7, the purple bar reaches approximately 26.7 and the yellow bar reaches approximately 24.8; for m=8, the purple bar reaches approximately 26.3 and the yellow bar reaches approximately 24.9; for m=9, the purple bar reaches approximately 26.6 and the yellow bar reaches approximately 25.2; and for m=10, the purple bar reaches approximately 26.4 and the yellow bar reaches approximately 24.4. The bars are not sorted by height; instead, they are grouped by m value, with the Fine-to-Coarse strategy bars appearing to the left of the Uniform strategy bars for each m. The chart includes a legend in the top right corner that distinguishes the two strategies by color. There are no visual annotations or emphasis on specific bars beyond their color-coded representation.
model_annotations.German: This bar chart compares the retrieval performance measured by MAP@10 for two sampling strategies—Fine-to-Coarse Sampling Strategy (represented by purple bars) and Uniform Sampling Strategy (represented by yellow bars)—across five different values of m, specifically m=6, 7, 8, 9, and 10. The horizontal axis, labeled "m", displays these discrete integer values in ascending order from left to right. The vertical axis, labeled "MAP@10", is scaled linearly from 23.0 to 27.0, with tick marks and labels at regular intervals of 0.5. For each value of m, two bars are presented side-by-side, with the purple bar for the Fine-to-Coarse strategy appearing to the left of the yellow bar for the Uniform strategy. The purple bars for m=6, 7, 8, 9, and 10 have approximate MAP@10 values of 25.99, 26.74, 26.32, 26.56, and 26.46 respectively. The yellow bars for the same m values have approximate MAP@10 values of 24.38, 24.77, 25.62, 25.25, and 24.37 respectively. The bars are not sorted by height, and no visual highlighting or special formatting is applied to any individual bar. The legend in the top right corner clearly distinguishes the two sampling strategies by color.
